His comments carry every clause: 知足知止 (content, knowing when to stop), 各修其內 (each tending what is within), 貪欲無厭 ... 各求於外 (insatiable greed seeking outside). Evidence is verbatim. The labels peaceful and warring describe the verse's two worlds, not a claim about Wang Bi. Plain sense: the chapter opens on the two horses and closes on the sufficiency of contentment, so a chapter in praise of contentment setting peace beside war is fair and not softened. verse.js ok (Tao Te Ching 46, at [45]); entry-check ok; 43 words.
